title: Detecting Lookahead Bias in LLM Forecasts

task.value: Develop a statistical test to detect lookahead bias (memorization of realized outcomes) in LLM-generated economic forecasts.
task.quote: We develop a statistical procedure to detect lookahead bias in economic forecasts generated by large language models (LLMs).

architecture.value: Date-only recall query (firm name, ticker, date) yields first-token probabilities P(up), P(down), P(unknown); LAP = P(up)+P(down). The forecast signal is interacted with LAP in an accuracy regression, and a positive interaction indicates contamination.
architecture.quote: Augmenting the regression with the LAP main effect and the interaction \hat{\mu}\times\text{LAP}^{P(\text{known})} does.

data.value: CRSP daily returns for NYSE/NASDAQ/AMEX common stocks; Compustat; Bloomberg News headlines (91,357 headlines, 1,587 firms); Thomson Reuters StreetEvents earnings call transcripts (106,994 firm-quarters, 3,920 firms).
data.quote: The in-sample dataset spans January 2012 to December 2023 and consists of 91,357 news headlines covering 1,587 unique companies. We also collect a calendar-year 2024 sample of 7,568 headlines for the post-cutoff out-of-sample placebo.

window.value: Stock news: in-sample Jan 2012–Dec 2023, out-of-sample 2024. Earnings calls: in-sample 2006Q1–2020Q4, out-of-sample 2023Q3–2024Q1 (recall quarters 2024Q1–2024Q3). The split is Llama-3.3-70B's December 2023 cutoff.
window.quote: The in-sample window (2006Q1–2020Q4) yields 106,994 matched firm-quarter observations from 3,920 unique U.S. publicly listed firms. We also collect 6,744 matched firm-quarters from 2023Q3 through 2024Q1 for the post-cutoff out-of-sample placebo.

models.value: Llama-3.3-70B (Meta, open-source), training cutoff December 2023, run locally with vLLM at temperature 0.
models.quote: Our analysis adopts Llama-3.3-70B, an open-source model released by Meta. Llama-3.3-70B has a publicly documented training-data knowledge cutoff of December 2023

baselines.value: LLM-only regressions replicating Lopez-Lira and Tang (2023) and Jha et al. (2024); horse race against the inner-confidence measure of Chen et al. (2024).
baselines.quote: A horse race against the inner-confidence measure of Chen et al. (2024) shows that LAP and inner confidence load on distinct components of LLM forecasting performance.

headline_result.value: Stock news in-sample: LLM×LAP interaction 0.162 (t=3.64); a one-SD increase in LAP raises the LLM marginal effect by 0.067 pp (about 32%). Capex: interaction 0.512 (t=2.01), about 12%. Both interactions are insignificant post-cutoff.
headline_result.quote: The interaction coefficient is positive and highly significant: \hat{\delta}=0.162 ( t=3.64 ).

uncertainty.value: t-statistics with standard errors clustered by date (news) or by firm (capex); firm/date fixed effects. Variability from batched GPU inference was verified to be negligible.
uncertainty.quote: All specifications include firm and date fixed effects, with standard errors clustered by date.

leakage_controls.value: The study's purpose is to detect lookahead bias. It uses a post-training-cutoff placebo (2024) in which LAP collapses and the interaction becomes insignificant, plus an outcome-blind recall query.
leakage_controls.quote: To validate that the in-sample \text{LLM}\times\text{LAP} amplification is driven by memorization rather than some other source of co-movement, we re-estimate the headline regressions on the out-of-sample window.

limitations.value: The test identifies only the sign of contamination, not its magnitude. It relies on maintained assumptions, including monotonicity of the conditional slope and the exclusion of γ=1.
limitations.quote: Proposition 1 delivers a qualitative, one-sided test: it identifies the sign of the scalar contamination loading \gamma , not its magnitude. We do not point-estimate \gamma

release.value: The detection procedure is provided as a downloadable CLAUDE.md instruction file. No location beyond 'available for download here' is given.
release.quote: The detection procedure is specified in a CLAUDE.md instruction file, available for download here.
